spots.name: Como Cathedral
spots.summary: Como Cathedral is the Catholic cathedral of the city of Como, Lombardy, Italy, and the seat of the Bishop of Como. It is dedicated to the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Casa del Fascio

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Casa del Fascio of Como, also called Palazzo Terragni, is a building located in Como, Italy, in the Piazza del Popolo, considered one of the masterpieces of Italian Modern Architecture.

spots.name: Villa Olmo
spots.summary: Villa Olmo is a neoclassical villa located in the city of Como, northern Italy.

spots.name: Chiasso
spots.summary: Chiasso is a town and a municipality in the district of Mendrisio in the canton of Ticino in Switzerland.

spots.name: Tempio Voltiano

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Tempio Voltiano is a museum in the city of Como, Lombardy, Italy, dedicated to the scientist Alessandro Volta (1745–1827).

spots.name: Villa Erba
spots.summary: Villa Erba is a 19th-century villa in Cernobbio, on the western shore of Lake Como in northern Italy. Its location is not far from the Villa d'Este luxury hotel in Cernobbio.

spots.name: Life Electric
spots.summary: Life Electric is a contemporary sculpture by Daniel Libeskind, dedicated to the physicist Alessandro Volta (1745–1827). Completed in 2015, it is installed on the breakwater in Lake Como, Como, Italy.

spots.name: Castello Baradello

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Castello Baradello is a military fortification located on a 430 m (1,410 ft) high hill next to the city of Como, northern Italy.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Faro Voltiano di Brunate
spots.summary: 29-m tower was erected in 1927 in honour of Alessandro Volta. Boasting some of the best views on the lake, this very high building will allow you to look down on the lake some 2000 feet below. The views are much better than from the free terrace below.

spots.name: Villa d'Este
spots.summary: The Villa d'Este, originally Villa del Garovo, is a Renaissance patrician residence in Cernobbio on the shores of Lake Como in northern Italy, close to the city of Como.

spots.name: War memorial in Como
spots.summary: The Monument to the Fallen is a war memorial on the shore of Lake Como, in Como, Italy.

spots.name: Basilica di San Fedele

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of San Fedele in Como is located in the city center. The present Romanesque church dates from 1120 and is dedicated to the Fidelis of Como.

spots.name: Basilica of Sant'Abbondio

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Sant'Abbondio is a Romanesque-style 11th-century Catholic basilica church located in Como, region of Lombardy, Italy.

spots.name: Villa Bernasconi

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Villa Bernasconi is a typical example of an independent villa with a turret in the Art Nouveau style. Located in Cernobbio, it was commissioned by the textile manufacturer Davide Bernasconi to the Milanese architect Alfredo Campanini.

spots.name: Teatro Sociale
spots.summary: Teatro Sociale is a theatre in Como, designed by architect Giuseppe Cusi following a decision by the local nobility that a new one was needed to replace the existing 1764/65 building which was regarded as outdated.

spots.name: Porta Torre
spots.summary: Porta Torre is a main fortified tower located in the town of Como, in Lombardy, northern Italy. It is 40 meters high and it was built in 1192, to defend the main entrance of the city.

spots.name: Villa Pliniana
spots.summary: Villa Pliniana is a villa originally built in 1573, on the site of a more modest pre-existing building, in the territory of the municipality of Torno, in the province of Como, on the right bank of the western branch of Lake Como.

spots.name: Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia
spots.summary: Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is a multi-use stadium in Como, Italy. It is primarily used for football matches as the home ground of Como 1907. The stadium has a capacity of 13,602 spectators.

spots.name: Giovio Series

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Giovio Series, also known as the Giovio Collection or Giovio Portraits, is a series of 484 portraits assembled by the 16th-century Italian Renaissance historian and biographer Paolo Giovio. It includes portraits of literary figures, rulers, statesmen and other dignitaries, many of which were done from life.

spots.name: Como Civic Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Pinacoteca Civica di Palazzo Volpi is the town art gallery on Via Diaz 84 in the town of Como, Lombardy, Italy. It is housed in the 17th-century Palazzo Volpi.

spots.summary: The Giuseppe Garibaldi Historical Museum was established in 1932 in Como, northern Italy. It is dedicated to Giuseppe Garibaldi in memory of his activities in the city 1866, and his role in the Unification of Italy.
